title: Hack Night by Purdue Hackers | Fall 2026
description: Making something you're proud of is incredibly rewarding. But it's really hard to do alone. Since 2013, Purdue Hackers has been a home for students who want to build, ship, and demo creative-technical projects together! Throughout the year, we support students with equipment, funding, mentorship, and resources to help them bring ambitious ideas to life. Every Friday night, we run Hack Night: a pop-up makerspace at the Bechtel Center where students from all disciplines come together to hang out, work on personal projects, and make things with friends. At the end of the year, we host The Show , our annual demo day where members share what they’ve built with hundreds of students, faculty, alumni, and industry sponsors. We also bring startup and creative culture to Purdue! We work with founders, engineers, artists, and companies to host AMAs, tech talks, workshops, and other really cool events together. Our current sponsors include OpenAI, Neuralink, Vercel, Sentry, Cloudflare, and more! Whether you’re already building something, want to start a project, or just want to meet other people who love making things, Purdue Hackers is for you. Learn more at https://purduehackers.com

title: Designing Student Loan Programs in a Risky Economy with Lance Lochner
description: The Purdue University Research Center in Economics invites you to our December economic policy luncheon. Please register to hear from a Purdue Dream Hire. Designing Student Loan Programs in a Risky Economy with Lance Lochner 11:30 a.m.-12:30 p.m. Eastern, Wednesday December 2, 2026, Rawls Hall, 3rd Floor Commons ,100 S. Grant Street, Purdue’s West Lafayette campus On average, a college education is a rewarding financial investment; yet, many students struggle in the labor market after leaving school. Some leave college with sizeable debts that are easily repaid under normal circumstances, while some find loan repayments overwhelming when luck turns against them. How do we provide enough credit to students who need it, and make sure loan obligations are repaid, on average, while providing students who face an unfavorable post-college labor market with the “insurance,” or repayment assistance, they need? Economic theory provides useful insights on the design of efficient student loan programs with empirical evidence slowly filling in the details needed to address these concerns. Professor of Economics Lance Lochner joined the Daniels School in 2026 as part of Purdue’s Moveable Dream Hires program. He is co-coordinator of the Markets Network of the Human Capital and Economic Opportunity Global Working Group, and has devoted much of his career to understanding human capital formation across the life cycle. Lochner’s major fields of concentration include labor economics, public economics, the economics of education and the economics of crime. Space is limited for PURCE luncheons, and registration is required. Please register by noon on Friday, November 27. We look forward to seeing you in Rawls Hall for a catered lunch, networking, and a Q&A with Lochner following his talk. Parking is available in the nearby Grant Street Parking Garage. Reach out to us with any questions at purce@purdue.edu and (765) 494-3782. Learn more about our research center at business.purdue.edu/centers/purce.

description: SEC Skills Academy The Sustainable Energy Club of Purdue (SEC) Skills Academy is a new learning initiative designed to help students build practical technical skills, explore new areas of engineering, and learn directly from experienced SEC members and industry professionals. By coordinating workshop topics and scheduling with ongoing branch activities and projects, participants can learn relevant skills at the same time they are most useful. Whether you are a current SEC member, a Purdue student interested in learning something new, or someone with little to no previous experience, you are welcome to join. Our goal is to create an accessible and collaborative environment where students can learn, ask questions, and gain hands-on skills that they can apply to classes, projects, SEC activities, and future careers. title: Executive Forum with Jennifer Richter, Vice President Supply Chain - Cleaning for The Clorox Company
description: The Executive Forum is open to the public, as seating permits, and provides opportunities for the exchange of ideas and discussion of topics and issues facing business and management. Jennifer Richter serves as the Vice President, Supply Chain for The Clorox Company's US Cleaning business unit. In this role, she leads the supply chain networks, operations, and talent that support some of the company’s most recognized household and professional cleaning brands. Her work sits at the intersection of strategies across business aspirations, suppliers, manufacturing, distribution, technology, innovation, and people leadership. The Clorox Company champions people to be well and thrive every single day. Founded in 1913 and headquartered in Oakland, California, Clorox is driven by consumer-centric innovation. From cleaning to food storage to natural personal care, the company is committed to delivering clearly superior experiences through its trusted brands including Brita®, Burt's Bees®, Clorox®, Fresh Step®, Glad®, Hidden Valley®, Kingsford®, Liquid-Plumr®, PineSol® and Purell® as well as international brands such as Chux®, Clorinda® and Poett®. With operations in about 25 countries and territories, Clorox products are sold in more than 100 countries, helping people around the world live happier, healthier lives. Having recently been named by Forbes as one of America’s Best Employers for Women 2026, Clorox is proud to be recognized for efforts and impact in areas such as corporate and social responsibility, leadership development, inclusion and diversity, and culture. Since joining The Clorox Company in 2000, Jennifer has held roles across Supply Chain Planning, Customer Service, Transportation Operations, Customer Logistics, and Manufacturing for multiple Clorox businesses. Jennifer is a passionate people leader who believes a leader’s most important responsibility is enabling others to succeed. She believes optimism is a force multiplier, principles matter more than rules, and that performance and engagement are strongest when people are able to apply their strengths. Within Supply Chain, she has implemented a leadership approach that is grounded in raising the bar while creating the clarity, confidence, and space teammates need to do their best work. With the core leadership principle of “everyone wants to succeed” in mind, she is dedicated to developing talent, implementing inclusive leadership, supply chain competency building, and career pathing for her team. Jennifer graduated from North Carolina State University with BS degrees in Chemical Engineering and Pulp & Paper Science. She lives in Atlanta, GA with her husband and two children. A local community advocate, she serves on the board of directors for the Chastain Park Conservancy, an organization dedicated to restoring, enhancing, maintaining and preserving Atlanta’s second largest public park. She also enjoys creating lifetime memories with her family and volunteering with her local faith-based organization.

title: ELEVATING YOUR ONLINE TEACHING JOURNEY WORKSHOPS: Assessing Online Learners
description: ELEVATING YOUR ONLINE TEACHING JOURNEY WORKSHOPS How often do instructors have the opportunity to discuss their online teaching experiences with their peers? The Elevating Your Online Teaching Journey workshops are designed to help instructors pause and focus on a specific online course—whether it’s one you’re developing for the first time or one you’ve taught for years. Through hands-on virtual workshops, attendees will engage with peers to explore the complexities of online teaching and learning. The Purdue University Online instructional design team will present evidence-based practices for online teaching and lead instructors in thoughtful dialogue about those practices. Together, each instructor will explore and select new strategies to help transform their online course. Assessing Online Learners What is the best way to assess learners online? title: Purdue Cricket League - Indoor
description: Purdue Cricket League — Indoor (PCLI) is a student-run indoor cricket tournament where Purdue students are split into teams of 10 and play 12-over matches per side using indoor-safe taped tennis balls (no leather balls) . Designed to help students bond, stay active, and stay connected to a favorite sport from back home, the event welcomes all skill levels and encourages mixed-gender teams. We provide stumps, cones, and scorekeeping with two volunteer umpires per game ; the club provides bats and optional protective gear (no metal spikes). Purdue students only (PUID required). Planned schedule: October 24th - December 12th at the Turf Recreation Exercise Center at different time slots, with round-robin group play into knockouts and a short awards closing. Safety measures include a first-aid kit at the score table, an AED location posted, and a clear emergency procedure in coordination with facility staff; spectators remain behind a marked safety buffer. Team captains register rosters in advance; free agents may be placed on composite teams. No alcohol, tobacco, or vaping; water only on courts/turf; venue rules apply.

Yuzhu’s clinical interests are depression and anxiety, international student adjustment, spiritual identity and emotional functioning, and trauma-related concerns. title: Hack Night by Purdue Hackers | Fall 2026
description: Making something you're proud of is incredibly rewarding. But it's really hard to do alone. Since 2013, Purdue Hackers has been a home for students who want to build, ship, and demo creative-technical projects together! Throughout the year, we support students with equipment, funding, mentorship, and resources to help them bring ambitious ideas to life. Every Friday night, we run Hack Night: a pop-up makerspace at the Bechtel Center where students from all disciplines come together to hang out, work on personal projects, and make things with friends. At the end of the year, we host The Show , our annual demo day where members share what they’ve built with hundreds of students, faculty, alumni, and industry sponsors. We also bring startup and creative culture to Purdue! We work with founders, engineers, artists, and companies to host AMAs, tech talks, workshops, and other really cool events together. Our current sponsors include OpenAI, Neuralink, Vercel, Sentry, Cloudflare, and more! Whether you’re already building something, want to start a project, or just want to meet other people who love making things, Purdue Hackers is for you. Learn more at https://purduehackers.com
